derived_by: dirtyloader.re.trace + memmap on the HEX image; transport by its NVIC-bracketed bpm store

0x600A376A.note: usb_midi_read's bl usb_midi_read_message (0x600A36BC): core reads the packet, raises ev_midi, and hands it on unless a handler took it

settings_row.note: SYSTEM SETTINGS' layout: a text template of 24 rows of 40 characters, fields in braces numbered by row in order (BACKLIGHT 0 .. KEY DELAY 11), and its colours 0x3C4 bytes on. Its enter passes both to 0x6009AF74(grid, text, colours) from the literal 0x60074018 (the colours' address, text = it - 0x3C4); 0x600739BC/C4 are getters' copies. Core points all three at a copy whose row 21, the first blank after the last field, is field row 12, coloured like THEME (row 7).

loader.note: core 0.3: the C loader goes in free flash past the image (ends 0x601DD400); its state and the loaded mods go in the ITCM tail after the firmware's ITCM code (0x29B40) up to the end of the 6 ITCM banks (GPR17 0xAAAAAFFF = 192 KB). MPU region 1 (ITCM, RASR 0x07080025, read-only) is made read/write by core_early. load_at is the bl 0x6008FDA8 in setup() just after the card is mounted (0x6007A3FC at 0x6007F0BC) and before audio starts or the autosave loads: core_load reads the card there, because SdFat calls after setup() broke the firmware's own card reads. SdFat: FsBaseFile::open 0x600A0894 on the SdFs volume 0x200376EC (sdk/include/m8-headless/fw.h).

sysex_handler.note: usbMIDI's partial SysEx handler pointer; the firmware sets it to 0x6009C0B9 in setup (0x600869B0). core_boot chains it for ev_sysex.

phrase_slots.note: the phrase view's vtable (RAM) +0x34 (bulk redraw: cut, clear, paste, interpolate, rotate, fill, transpose) and +0x38 (a cell edited); core wraps them for ev_step_edit's bulk reports

BOOT.note: main(): bl setup; BOOT handlers run once after setup() returns

TICK.note: main(): bl loop; TICK handlers run before every loop()

DRAW.note: loop(): bl frame_refresh(display 0x2001A4F4), after the screen's update (0x6004A820 -> view +0x0C) and before the frame goes out

KEY.note: loop(): bl ui_input(ui 0x2001C1A4, action); action = the chord's key bits (EDIT 01 OPT 02 RIGHT 04 PLAY 08 SHIFT 10 DOWN 20 UP 40 LEFT 80)

VIEW.note: set_view(ui, id): leaves the old screen, fw_views[id] (0x20000B24, 30 slots, 7 empty), enters the new one

SONG_LOAD.note: the song loader (songs 0x2001C8FC, path, flag): the AUTOSAVE at setup() and every LOAD

SONG_SAVE.note: the song writer (?, path, ...): writes M8VERSION and the song to path

NOTE.note: note on, ITCM (load 0x6002425C): (player, instrument, ...) at the start of every note: from playback (via 0x269B8, the per-track pending-instrument poll), preview (0x23374) and row fire (0x23A7C); the note and velocity go to player +0x21C / +0x21E just after. Players are 0x2001ADF0 + 0x248 x track. Checked on hardware: one call per played note.

PLAY.note: the sequencer starts: sets the play flag (sequencer object 0x2000BE80 + 0x3B8 = 1), (seq, mode)

STOP.note: the sequencer stops: clears the play flag; called from 0x60088E3C

SERIAL.note: the m8c command parser (obj): drains USB serial into a 6-byte buffer and runs E/R/D/C/K/P/S. Called from loop and from the render screens' polling (24 sites); core's handler takes requests that start with 0xD1.

MIDI_OUT.note: usb_midi_write_packed(packet): every USB MIDI packet the M8 sends (clock, notes, CCs, SysEx)

TEMPO.note: set_tempo(clock_owner, float bpm): bpm in s0, stored at [[0x60090A10]]+0x3C0 inside AudioNoInterrupts

SEQ_TICK.note: the tick processor (load 0x600230E4), r0 = sequencer engine 0x2001ADDC; called once per sub-tick (192 a beat) by the clock node's drain (run 0x21CF4, only call 0x6002339E); it runs the 8 per-track updates. Ported from Model:02 0x60024B7C.

NOTE_OFF.note: note off (load 0x60024140): (player, 0 release / 1 kill); calls the instrument's vt+0x1C. Reached from the player tick (OFF 0x80, KIL countdown), row fire before a retrigger, and key release. Model:02 0x25BB0.

ROW.note: the sequencer's row fire, inside the per-track update 0x24650 (load 0x600261FC): reached only on a new row; r4 = player, the 9-byte row at [player+0x4C]; note-on and the FX applier follow.

FX_ROW.note: phrase FX applier (load 0x60024464), 72 cases: (player, column 0-2, cmd, value, [sp] flag). Model:02 0x25ED4.

FX_COMMAND.note: table FX executor (load 0x60026F6C), 78 cases (cmp r8,#0x4D; tbh): (table runner, column, cmd, value, [sp] flag); called from the dispatch wrapper 0x263F4. Model:02 0x287A4.

MOD_APPLY@FM.note: FM: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@HYPER.note: HYPER: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@MACRO.note: MACRO: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@SAMPLER.note: SAMPLER: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@WAV.note: WAV: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@EXTERNAL.note: EXTERNAL: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MOD_APPLY@SAMPLER0.note: SAMPLER0: the modulation destination switch (subs/cmp before the tbb/tbh); taken goes to the shared epilogue, as an out-of-range destination does. Model:02 port.

MUTE.note: apply a track's mute/solo (mixer 0x2000C260, track 0-7): every mute/solo path calls it for each of the 8 tracks; mute mask mixer+0x1B0, solo mask +0x1B4

INST_LOAD.note: load an .m8i into a slot (songs 0x2001C8FC, path, slot, 0)

INST_SAVE.note: save a slot to an .m8i (songs, path, slot)

PARAM_SET.note: the instrument view's field changed (instview, field, old): pushes the value to the playing tracks; new value **(view+8), slot view+0xC

STEP_EDIT.note: the phrase view's cell-edited method (vt+0x38): (view, cell, n, column, [sp] row); phrase *(u8*)(view+4). Bulk edits (clear, paste) may not reach it.

INST_CLEAR.note: clear an instrument slot (song 0x2025F674, slot, full): the pool's delete, and the instrument loader before it loads

LIVE_NOTE.note: the live / preview note trigger (load 0x600249F4): (player, instrument, note, velocity; stack: phrase, row, flag). Its callers are the UI's (13 flash sites through the veneer 0x600A8DC0: entering and auditioning notes, previews) and a chord helper; the sequencer fires rows elsewhere (ev_row). Model:02 0x24DE0.

INST_COPY.note: clone an instrument (instview 0x2001A530, src, dst): the phrase and table views' SHIFT+EDIT on an instrument cell ('CLONED INSTRUMENT %02X TO %02X')

INST_PASTE.note: paste the copied instrument (instview, action): the instrument view's and the pool's SHIFT+EDIT after SHIFT+OPT; ldrb/cmp then beq.w at +4

notes: loop (0x6007F02C) is a b.w veneer to the real loop at 0x6007FC54.
Headless is a different build from Model:02 6.6.2A: the clock is no longer a fixed global (bpm sits at +0x3C0 of an object reached through a pointer), so 6.6.2A addresses do not carry over.
Pin 13 (GPIO7 bit 3, the Teensy LED) is not used by this firmware; it drives GPIO7 bit 10 (pin 6) in setup().
